problem: Running specialized AI tasks via commercial APIs (Claude, GPT, etc.) is expensive at scale and in perpetuity. Teams with recurring, well-defined AI tasks — classification, extraction, summarization — pay the same per-request cost on day 1,000 as on day 1, even though the task is stable and predictable. Local/fine-tuned models alone lack the quality ceiling of frontier models, so teams stay locked in. What's needed is a system that starts with the best frontier model, progressively teaches a local model to replicate its outputs for specific tasks, then adaptively withdraws the expensive dependency — while maintaining quality guarantees and enforcing hard budget limits. The caller should never know or care which model answered; they submit a request and get a response through a single unified interface.

places.name: CLI / Library Entry
places.description: The caller's surface: either 'apprentice' CLI command or 'from apprentice import Apprentice' library import. Loads config, boots the system.

places.name: Config Loader
places.description: Parses and strictly validates apprentice.yaml at startup. Fails fast with clear errors on invalid config. Produces typed Pydantic models for all downstream components.

places.name: Task Registry
places.description: Holds the set of configured task types, each with name, description, input/output schema, prompt templates, evaluator type, match fields, and confidence thresholds.

places.name: Unified Interface
places.description: The single async function/class that accepts a task name + input dict and returns a typed result. The caller has no visibility into which model produced the answer.

places.name: Router
places.description: Decides per-request whether to send to remote, local, or both. Consults the Confidence Engine for current phase and the Sampling Scheduler for whether this request is a coaching sample.

places.name: Remote API Client
places.description: Abstraction over Anthropic/OpenAI/Google APIs. Handles auth (from env vars), retries with exponential backoff, error recovery. Tracks per-request cost for budget accounting. Supports primary + optional additional providers for training diversity.

places.name: Local Model Server
places.description: Abstraction over Ollama/vLLM/llama.cpp. Handles model loading, version swapping on promotion, health checks. Returns a clear 'unavailable' status in Phase 1 when no model exists yet.

places.name: Confidence Engine
places.description: Per-task quality tracker. Maintains a rolling window of comparison-pair samples (configurable size, default 100 pairs). Computes correlation as per-field match rate averaged across match_fields (structured_match) or cosine similarity (semantic_similarity). Detects drift (gradual) and shift (sudden). Derives current phase from correlation score and training example count. Enforces time-based staleness safety net (max_window_age).

places.name: Sampling Scheduler
places.description: Given the current correlation from the Confidence Engine, outputs whether THIS request should be a coaching sample (sent to both models). Sampling rate is a continuous function of correlation — configurable as exponential decay, linear, or step. Has a hard minimum floor (e.g., 2%). Forces 100% sampling when confidence drops below coaching_trigger. Reverts to full remote below emergency_threshold.

places.name: Training Data Store
places.description: Collects and persists input + remote response pairs as training examples. Tracks count per task type. Holds out a configurable percentage as a validation/test set. Signals when batch size threshold is reached.

places.name: Training Pipeline
places.description: Orchestrates fine-tuning when sufficient examples accumulate. Supports plugin backends: Unsloth/Axolotl (local LoRA), OpenAI fine-tuning API, Hugging Face. For Ollama deployment: manages train → quantize → GGUF conversion → Ollama model registration. Validates new model against held-out test set before promotion. Keeps current model version on failure.

places.name: Budget Manager
places.description: Enforces hard spending limits: per-task, daily, weekly, monthly caps. Tracks actual remote API spend and estimated local savings. When budget is exhausted: in Phase 1 raises BudgetExhaustedError; in Phase 2/3 forces local-only mode with logged warning. Never exceeds limits.

places.name: Reporting & Observability
places.description: Exposes current phase per task, confidence scores and trends, sampling frequency history, correlation over time, cost breakdown (remote vs local compute), alerts on quality degradation or budget warnings. Outputs as JSON, CLI summary, or optional webhook.

places.name: Audit Log
places.description: Structured JSON log of every decision: which model served each request, routing reason, confidence at time of decision, cost incurred, training events, model promotions, phase transitions. Machine-readable audit trail.

affordances.name: load_config
affordances.description: Parse and validate apprentice.yaml, produce typed config objects

affordances.name: submit_request
affordances.description: Caller sends task_name + input_dict through unified interface

affordances.name: route_request
affordances.description: Router decides: remote-only, local-only, or both (coaching sample)

affordances.name: call_remote
affordances.description: Send prompt to primary remote API, receive response, track cost

affordances.name: call_remote_additional
affordances.description: Optionally send to additional providers for training data diversity

affordances.name: call_local
affordances.description: Send prompt to local model server, receive response

affordances.name: check_local_health
affordances.description: Verify local model server is running and a model is loaded

affordances.name: evaluate_pair
affordances.description: Compare local vs remote response using task-specific evaluator, produce per-field scores

affordances.name: update_confidence
affordances.description: Push new comparison sample into rolling window, recompute correlation and phase

affordances.name: compute_sampling_rate
affordances.description: Derive current coaching sample frequency from correlation trend

affordances.name: check_staleness
affordances.description: Verify oldest sample in window hasn't exceeded max_window_age; force coaching if stale

affordances.name: store_training_example
affordances.description: Persist input + remote response pair to training data store

affordances.name: trigger_fine_tune
affordances.description: Launch fine-tuning job when batch size threshold met

affordances.name: validate_new_model
affordances.description: Run held-out test set against new model, check quality threshold

affordances.name: promote_model
affordances.description: Swap local model server to new fine-tuned version

affordances.name: convert_to_gguf
affordances.description: Run train → quantize → GGUF → Ollama registration pipeline

affordances.name: check_budget
affordances.description: Verify spend hasn't exceeded any cap before making remote call

affordances.name: record_spend
affordances.description: Log cost of remote API call against budget tracker

affordances.name: report_status
affordances.description: Output current phase, confidence, cost, sampling frequency per task

affordances.name: log_decision
affordances.description: Write structured audit entry for every routing and training decision

affordances.name: raise_budget_exhausted
affordances.description: Return BudgetExhaustedError when no budget remains and no local model exists

affordances.name: force_local_only
affordances.description: Switch to local-only mode when budget exhausted but local model available

affordances.name: escalate_coaching
affordances.description: Increase sampling to 100% and optionally trigger retraining when anti-correlation detected

connections.description: Boot sequence starts by parsing config
Validated config populates task registry
Caller submits task_name + input through unified interface
Interface delegates to router for model selection
Router queries confidence engine for current phase and correlation
Router queries scheduler to determine if this request is a coaching sample
Router checks budget before routing to remote
Phase 1: all requests; Phase 2: all requests; Phase 3: coaching samples only
Phase 2: all requests (for comparison); Phase 3: all requests
Router verifies local model is available before routing to it
Every remote call records its cost
Every remote response becomes a training example
Optionally fan out to additional providers for training diversity
When both local and remote respond, engine scores the comparison
Updated correlation feeds into sampling rate computation
Periodic check that rolling window hasn't gone stale
Anti-correlation triggers coaching escalation
Batch size threshold reached, trigger fine-tuning
For Ollama backend: train → quantize → GGUF → register
New model validated against held-out test set
Validated model swapped into serving
No budget + no local model = clear error to caller
Budget exhausted but local model exists = local-only mode
Every routing decision is logged with context
Training events and model promotions are logged
Phase transitions and confidence changes are logged
Reporting reads from confidence engine for current state
Reporting reads from budget manager for cost data
Reporting reads audit log for history and trends

rabbit_holes.description: GGUF conversion pipeline complexity: The train → quantize → GGUF → Ollama registration pipeline involves multiple tools (Unsloth, llama.cpp quantize, Ollama create) with version-sensitive compatibility. Format mismatches or tool version skew could consume the entire budget of time.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Constrain Milestone 1 to a single tested backend combination (e.g., Unsloth LoRA → llama.cpp GGUF Q4_K_M → Ollama). Pin tool versions. Build the pipeline as a shell-out with clear error messages rather than deep Python integration. Mark other combinations as 'experimental' behind a config flag. Write integration tests against known-good artifacts.

rabbit_holes.description: Correlation metric is too simple for nuanced tasks: Per-field match rate works for exact-match fields like 'category' but breaks down for free-text, numeric ranges, or partially correct outputs. Teams may lose trust if the confidence score doesn't reflect perceived quality.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Ship with three evaluator types (exact_match, structured_match, semantic_similarity) and a 'custom' evaluator hook that accepts a Python callable path in config. Keep the built-in evaluators dead simple and well-documented. Custom evaluators are the escape hatch — they receive (local_output, remote_output, task_config) and return a float 0-1. This way we don't over-engineer the built-in evaluators.

rabbit_holes.description: Semantic similarity requires an embedding model: The semantic_similarity evaluator needs sentence-transformers and a model like all-MiniLM-L6-v2. This adds a heavyweight ML dependency to a system that otherwise has minimal deps. Loading the model has startup cost and memory impact.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Make sentence-transformers an optional dependency — only imported when a task uses semantic_similarity evaluator. Fail fast at config validation time if the evaluator is configured but the dependency isn't installed. Document this clearly. The base system runs with zero ML dependencies if only structured_match/exact_match evaluators are used.

rabbit_holes.description: Phase 1 budget exhaustion is a dead end: If the budget runs out before enough training examples are collected (phase1_to_phase2 threshold not met), the system has no local model to fall back to. It must return errors for every request until budget resets. This could be days.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: This is the intended behavior per the interview (raise BudgetExhaustedError). But we should make it highly visible: prominent warning in reporting when budget burn rate projects exhaustion before phase1_to_phase2 threshold, so operators can adjust budgets or thresholds before hitting the wall. Add a 'projected_phase1_completion' metric to reporting.

rabbit_holes.description: Rolling window staleness in low-traffic deployments: At 2% sampling floor, reaching 100 comparison pairs requires ~5000 requests. Low-traffic tasks might take weeks/months to fill the window, during which the confidence score is based on stale data and the system can't detect drift.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Implement the time-based staleness safety net from the interview: if the oldest sample exceeds max_window_age (configurable, default 24h), force a coaching sample regardless of sampling schedule. Also, allow the window to operate with fewer than window_size samples (compute confidence from whatever's available) with a 'low_sample_warning' flag in reporting.

rabbit_holes.description: Fine-tuning takes hours, blocks Phase 2 graduation: LoRA fine-tuning on even a modest dataset can take 30-60+ minutes on consumer GPUs. During this time, the system is stuck in Phase 1. If fine-tuning fails, the system stays in Phase 1 indefinitely.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Fine-tuning runs asynchronously (background process). The system continues serving from remote during training. Training state is persisted so it survives restarts. On failure: log error, keep current state, retry on next batch accumulation. Add training_status to reporting (idle / in_progress / failed / succeeded).

rabbit_holes.description: Prompt template design determines training quality: The same prompt template is used for both remote and local models, but they may have very different instruction-following capabilities. A prompt optimized for Claude may produce poor results when replayed against a fine-tuned Llama 8B.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: Allow separate prompt_template and local_prompt_template in task config. Default to using the same template. Document that prompt engineering for the local model is a key tuning lever. The training pipeline stores the prompt used with each example so the local model is fine-tuned on prompts it will actually see.

rabbit_holes.description: Scope creep into a full MLOps platform: The spec touches training, serving, evaluation, versioning, budgeting, and reporting. Each of these is a product in its own right. Without firm boundaries the project balloons.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: The phased delivery approach (Milestone 1: cold-start pipeline, Milestone 2: adaptive behavior, Milestone 3: governance) constrains scope per cycle. Each milestone has a clear 'done' definition. Features not in the current milestone go to the backlog, not into the code. The no-gos list is the boundary.

rabbit_holes.description: Model validation before promotion can't guarantee production quality: The held-out test set is drawn from historical remote responses. If the task's input distribution shifts (new ticket categories, new entity types), the test set becomes unrepresentative and a model could pass validation but fail in production.
rabbit_holes.mitigation: The ongoing Phase 3 sampling is the real safety net — it continuously monitors production quality. The held-out test set is a pre-promotion gate, not the only quality check. Document that the test set should be periodically refreshed (future enhancement). The emergency_threshold → revert-to-remote behavior is the hard safety net.

no_gos: No ensembling or merging of local and remote outputs — always one-or-the-other, never blended
No concurrent/parallel request handling — one request at a time, casual pace
No runtime config hot-reloading — restart required for config changes
No general-purpose model training framework — only the specific distillation lifecycle
No chatbot or conversational AI support — structured, defined task operations only
No model marketplace — one local model per task type, period
No real-time latency optimization — seconds per response is acceptable
No request queuing when budget is exhausted in Phase 1 — raise BudgetExhaustedError honestly
No round-robin serving across multiple remote providers — primary provider serves all live requests
No GPU or API key requirement for tests — all external boundaries mocked
No dependency on Pact or any parent framework — fully standalone
